title: Immersive dark-mode: surface fusion and component adapters
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Summary: This ticket captures a focused design effort to establish an 'immersive' dark-mode variant for the Redwood Console that reduces perceptual noise while preserving brand accents and component affordances. Scope: token mappings for surfaces, elevation harmonization across cards/tables/charts, compact/button interaction overrides, and a small set of component adapters for third-party charting libs. Out of scope: full internationalization pass, A/B rollout automation (handled by Console runtime team). Goals:
- Create a small, opinionated surface palette (surface-fusion) that reduces contrast collisions on deep backgrounds while keeping brand accents legible.
- Define component-level adapters that apply safe swaps vs. destructive token overrides (buttons, tables, progress/stepper, and chart axis/grid).
- Provide a migration guide for engineering: token rename map, fallback rules, and recommended CSS variables for runtime toggles.

Design constraints and considerations:
- Many customers use dedicated/private deployments with strict theming needs; the variant must be configurable via tokens and not require code changes.
- Charts: avoid color breaks for stacked series; prefer perceptually uniform adjustments (HSL/OKLCH approach) over arbitrary darkened colors.
- Performance: token set should be small (<= 24 new tokens) and rely on cascade-friendly CSS variables to avoid runtime recomputation.
- Accessibility: aim for AA on core surfaces and buttons; provide notes where AAA is not achievable given brand constraints.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Surface token set merged into design tokens file with clear naming: --surface-immersive-0..3, --surface-foreground-immersive, --brand-accent-immersive.
2) Component adapters documented with before/after screenshots for Button (primary/secondary/ghost), Table (header/row/striping), and Chart (grid/axis/legend).
3) Figma component library updated and linked; engineering has a token rename map and a one-page migration guide.
4) Design review approvals from PM and Eng leads recorded in ticket comments.
5) Small visual regression suite (screenshots) authored and handed to QA for smoke tests.
updates: 2026-02-20: Ticket created during theming sync; prioritized for the cycle. (Asha)
2026-02-24: Initial exploratory frames posted to Figma: two direction candidates (soft-fusion and deep-ink). Shared with PM for preference. (Asha)
2026-02-27: PM prefers soft-fusion for consistency with existing console density. Added ENG-39402 dependency to coordinate token rollout gating. (Marco)
2026-03-03: Prototype built in Storybook using runtime CSS variables. Early findings: chart grid contrasts required a separate axis token to avoid washed-out series. Logged as action item. (Marco)

2026-03-08: Design review with frontend: agreed on token naming, decided to expose immersive tokens as an opt-in theme key (theme: 'immersive-dark') to avoid breaking default dark. Engineer note: PR for token file expected by 2026-03-15. (Asha, Marco)
2026-03-10: Added migration guide draft and screenshot set for button/table components. Seeking final PM sign-off. (Asha)
